reference: Zhang and Far, Beneficial and detrimental impacts of soil-structure interaction on seismic response of high-rise buildings
external_evidence_type: finite-element study verified by shaking-table tests; large parametric matrix
comparable_quantity: base-shear ratio, inter-storey drift ratio, period elongation
published_result_or_extractable_signal: 720 flexible-base cases; normalized base shear and drift ratios; reported foundation rotation increases drift while base shear can reduce; natural-period tables allow lambda/eta extraction
relationship_to_article_116: Directly supports the mixed force-beneficial/displacement-detrimental mechanism and can be mapped onto the article's RV and lambda framework
usable_score_effect: Can strengthen validation/comparison from 13.5 to about 14.0 if used as external quantitative consistency mapping; higher only if figure/table data are digitized case by case
claim_boundary: Consistency mapping, not independent validation of the demand-polarity map predictions

reference: Yang et al., Effects of soil-structure interaction on the seismic response of RC frame-shear wall building structures under far-field long-period ground motions
comparable_quantity: base-shear influence coefficient, top-displacement coefficient, maximum inter-story drift coefficient
published_result_or_extractable_signal: Base-shear SSI coefficient reported in the 0.5-1 range; displacement and drift coefficients reported greater than 1 and less than 3; long-period motions can also produce shear amplification in bimodal spectra
relationship_to_article_116: Strong external quantitative support for the article's separation of force benefit from displacement penalty and for the warning that spectral position controls polarity
usable_score_effect: Can strengthen external comparison by adding a numerical range check rather than another citation
claim_boundary: Not a validation of the reduced closed-form formula; it is a cross-study range and mechanism check

reference: Tao, Fu and Li, The possibility of detrimental effects on soil-structure interaction in seismic design due to a shift in system frequency
external_evidence_type: analytical and time-domain SSI study using building/site cases and earthquake records
comparable_quantity: system-frequency shift and detrimental response occurrence
published_result_or_extractable_signal: Shows SSI can be detrimental depending on structure-soil-earthquake combination; uses four California buildings and 42 earthquake records in the time-domain study
relationship_to_article_116: Supports the article's spectral-shift logic and the need to treat period elongation as conditionally beneficial rather than automatically safe
usable_score_effect: Improves discussion and limitation strength; useful as qualitative-to-semiquantitative external consistency evidence
claim_boundary: Does not directly provide article-116 class predictions or RV/error pairs

reference: Mylonakis and Gazetas, Seismic soil-structure interaction: Beneficial or detrimental?
published_result_or_extractable_signal: Shows that the code-style assumption that period elongation plus damping invariably reduces forces is not generally valid; certain seismic and soil environments make SSI detrimental
relationship_to_article_116: Foundational support for the article's premise and for the mixed/detrimental polarity taxonomy
usable_score_effect: Strengthens scientific framing but should not be counted as new validation data
claim_boundary: Conceptual/theoretical external support, not a case-level benchmark

reference: Tileylioglu, Stewart and Nigbor, Dynamic stiffness and damping of a shallow foundation from forced vibration of a field test structure
external_evidence_type: field forced-vibration test at Garner Valley SFSI structure
comparable_quantity: foundation stiffness, damping, frequency dependence, impedance consistency
published_result_or_extractable_signal: Experimental impedance ordinates are generally consistent with numerical models when soil moduli are adjusted and hysteretic damping is considered; damping increases strongly with frequency
relationship_to_article_116: Supports the physical plausibility of frequency-dependent stiffness/damping and the Garner Valley instrumentation/provenance layer
usable_score_effect: Useful as field-mechanics support, but it does not increase class-level predictive validation by itself
claim_boundary: Field impedance support only; not nonlinear 3D response-history validation
